mainTopic: Vowing a תודה and its loaves from different kinds of money (חולין versus מעשר שני), and רב הונא's rule that someone who vows only 'loaves of a תודה' must bring the whole offering
overview: The משנה lists ways to vow a קרבן תודה and its loaves using ordinary money (חולין) or מעשר שני money. If the animal is from חולין and the loaves from מעשר, both must come from חולין. If the animal is from מעשר, he may bring it as he said. Any מעשר used for the loaves must be מעשר שני coins, not מעשר שני wheat. רב הונא rules that vowing 'loaves of a תודה' obligates the whole offering. The גמרא defends him against challenges from the משנה and from a ברייתא that forces someone who vowed 'a תודה without loaves' to bring both. The גמרא then asks why that vow is not simply cancelled as a mistake. חזקיה says the ברייתא follows בית שמאי's rule of going by the first words. רבי יוחנן says it can fit בית הלל too, and אביי and רבא explain the פסוק 'שמור ושמעת'. Finally רב נחמן and רב חסדא allow loaves made from wheat bought with מעשר שני money. רבי זירא disagrees and begins laying out the reasoning on both sides, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Thanks offering from ordinary money, loaves from tithe money
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that someone who vows a תודה from חולין and its loaves from מעשר must bring both from חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone says: 'I take upon myself a thanks offering from non-sacred money, and its loaves from tithe money', he must bring the offering and its loaves from non-sacred money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its first case: the person wants the animal from ordinary money and the loaves from מעשר שני money. The משנה rules that both must come from ordinary money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first words already obligated him in a full תודה from חולין, and the loaves belong to that offering. So his added request to use מעשר money for the loaves does not work, and everything comes from חולין.

keyTerms.meaning: The thanks offering, an animal brought together with forty loaves
Its loaves, meaning the loaves that go with the תודה
Ordinary, non-sacred money or food
Here, מעשר שני, the second tithe, which must be eaten or spent in ירושלים

phrases.english: "A thanks offering is upon me from non-sacred money,
and its loaves from tithe money"
phrases.notes: "Tithe" here means מעשר שני money, which a person normally spends on food in ירושלים.

phrases.english: he must bring it and its loaves from non-sacred money.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹדָה עָלַי מִן הַחוּלִּין וְלַחְמָהּ מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of a תודה from חולין with loaves from מעשר requires both the תודה and the loaves from חולין.

steps.title: Thanks offering from tithe money with loaves from either source
steps.stepSummary: If he vows the תודה from מעשר and the loaves from חולין, or both from מעשר, he may bring it as he said.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he says 'a thanks offering from tithe money and its loaves from non-sacred money', he may bring it that way. If he says 'it and its loaves from tithe money', he may bring it that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two more cases, and in both the person may bring the offering exactly as he vowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the animal itself was assigned to מעשר money from the start. Paying for the loaves with חולין, or with מעשר as well, does not take away from the main offering, so his words are followed.

keyTerms.meaning: He may bring, meaning he may do it the way he said

steps.confusionAlert: Notice the reversal. Animal from חולין plus loaves from מעשר does NOT work (step 1). Animal from מעשר plus loaves from חולין DOES work.

phrases.english: "A thanks offering from tithe money
and its loaves from non-sacred money": he may bring it that way.
"It and its loaves from tithe money": he may bring it that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹדָה מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר וְלַחְמָהּ מִן הַחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of vow cases with the opposite arrangement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תודה from מעשר, with loaves from either חולין or מעשר, may be brought as vowed.

steps.title: Loaves bought with tithe coins, not baked from tithe wheat
steps.stepSummary: Loaves paid for with מעשר must come from מעשר שני money, not from מעשר שני wheat.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he may not bring the loaves from second-tithe wheat, only from second-tithe money.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a detail about how the מעשר is used. He buys the flour with מעשר שני coins and does not use wheat that is itself מעשר שני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets a limit on the earlier cases. Even when מעשר may be used, it has to be מעשר שני money that buys the flour, not the actual tithe wheat.

keyTerms.meaning: Wheat that is itself מעשר שני produce
Coins that the מעשר שני produce was exchanged for

steps.whatToRemember: In the משנה, an animal from חולין makes everything חולין. An animal from מעשר lets you follow your words. Any מעשר used must be מעשר שני money.

phrases.english: And he may not bring them from second-tithe wheat,
but only from second-tithe money.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יָבִיא מֵחִיטֵּי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits how the מעשר allowed in step 2 may be used.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Loaves funded by מעשר must be bought with מעשר שני coins, not made from מעשר שני wheat.

steps.title: Vowing only loaves still requires the full thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that someone who vows 'loaves of a תודה' must bring the animal and the loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: One who says 'I take upon myself loaves of a thanks offering' must bring a thanks offering and its loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a new ruling from רב הונא. Even though the person mentioned only the loaves, he has to bring the whole תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words seem to cover only bread, but רב הונא reads them as a vow for the complete offering. The next step explains why.

keyTerms.meaning: "It is upon me", the standard wording for accepting a vow
The loaves of a thanks offering

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna said:
One who says: "It is upon me to bring loaves of a thanks offering"
must bring a thanks offering and its loaves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא הָאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי לַחְמֵי תוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא with a related ruling about the wording of vows for a תודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow for 'loaves of a תודה' obligates the person in the full תודה with its loaves.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is what the גמרא will test against the משנה in the next steps.

steps.title: Why vowing loaves means vowing the whole offering
steps.stepSummary: The person knows loaves are never offered without the animal, so he really meant both. He only mentioned the last part.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? This man knows that loaves are not offered without a thanks offering, so he was really saying 'a thanks offering and its loaves'. He said 'loaves of a thanks offering' because he mentioned the end of the matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב הונא rules this way and answers right away. The man knew bread alone is never offered, so he must have meant the whole תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His vow cannot mean bread by itself, because that is impossible. So we read it as the full offering. He named the loaves only because they are the last part of the process.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
He surely knows
He mentioned the end of the matter

phrases.english: What is the reason?
This man surely knows
that loaves are not offered without a thanks offering,
so this man is saying "a thanks offering and its loaves,"
and the fact that he said "loaves of a thanks offering"
is because he mentioned the end of the matter.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא מִידָּע יָדַע הַאי גַּבְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind רב הונא's ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why a vow for loaves alone obligates the full תודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He knows loaves are never offered alone, so his words mean the whole offering. He just named the final part.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה against רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: If 'loaves' means the whole offering, then 'its loaves from חולין' should make the whole תודה come from חולין. Yet the משנה lets him bring it as he vowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'A thanks offering from tithe money and its loaves from non-sacred money: he brings it as he vowed.' But why? Since he said 'its loaves from non-sacred money', he should bring the offering and its loaves from non-sacred money!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא from the second case of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא says that mentioning loaves equals vowing the full offering. If so, 'its loaves from חולין' should count as a new vow for a whole תודה with loaves from חולין. Yet the משנה lets the animal come from מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: As he vowed
And why? Used here to raise a difficulty

phrases.english: We learned in the Mishna: A thanks offering from tithe money
and its loaves from non-sacred money
he brings it as he vowed.
But why?
Since he said "its loaves from non-sacred money,"
he should bring it and its loaves from non-sacred money!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן תּוֹדָה מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר וְלַחְמָהּ מִן הַחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רב הונא's ruling against the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's rule that mentioning loaves of a תודה equals vowing the full offering.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By רב הונא's logic, 'its loaves from חולין' should be a vow for a full תודה from חולין. That contradicts the משנה, which allows the animal from מעשר.

steps.title: His loaves refer to the offering he already named
steps.stepSummary: Since he first said 'a תודה from מעשר', his words about the loaves are just loaves for that offering, like loaves vowed to complete someone else's תודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there. Since he first said 'a thanks offering from tithe money', he is like someone who says 'I take upon myself loaves to exempt so-and-so's thanks offering'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא by showing that the משנה's case is different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא's rule applies only when the loaves are vowed with no offering already named. In the משנה, the תודה was already set from מעשר, so 'its loaves' clearly means bread for that animal. That is like vowing loaves to complete another person's תודה, which obligates only the loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there
He is treated as one who says
To exempt the thanks offering of so-and-so, meaning to supply its loaves

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא: vowing 'loaves of a תודה' with no offering named means the whole offering. If an offering was already named, the loaves just belong to it.

phrases.english: It is different there,
since he said "a thanks offering from tithe money,"
he is like one who says:
"It is upon me to bring loaves
to exempt the thanks offering of so-and-so."

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם דְּכֵיוָן דְּאָמַר תּוֹדָה מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The challenge assumed that 'its loaves from חולין' works as a new vow for a full תודה from חולין.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once the תודה was already set from מעשר, the loaves are only bread for that offering, so רב הונא's rule does not apply.

steps.title: Apply the same logic to the first case of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: If a vow for loaves can mean loaves to complete someone else's תודה, then in the רישא a vow for a תודה should mean an animal to complete someone else's loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the first case of the משנה: 'a תודה from חולין and its loaves from מעשר.' There he must bring both from חולין. But by your logic, he should count as someone who said 'I take on a תודה to complete so-and-so's loaves.' Then only the animal would need to be חולין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the answer from Step 7 and tries it on the first case of the משנה, where it seems to give the wrong result.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 7, the loaves were treated as a separate item that completes someone else's תודה. If that works, then an animal vowed from חולין should also be a separate item that completes someone else's loaves, and the loaves could come from מעשר. But the משנה says everything must come from חולין, so the answer seems to fail.

keyTerms.meaning: The first clause of the משנה
Ordinary, non-sacred money or food
To exempt, meaning here to complete someone else's obligation
So-and-so, some other person

phrases.english: If so,
the first clause, which teaches:
"A תודה from non-sacred money
and its loaves from מעשר"
he must bring it and its loaves from non-sacred money;
here too, let him be considered like one who says
"It is upon me to bring a תודה
to exempt the loaves of so-and-so"!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, רֵישָׁא דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of Step 7 by applying its logic to the רישא of the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 7 that a vow for loaves can mean loaves to complete another person's תודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Make the same move in reverse: the vowed animal completes someone else's loaves. That would let the loaves come from מעשר, which contradicts the משנה's ruling.

steps.title: Loaves complete a תודה, but a תודה never completes loaves
steps.stepSummary: The comparison fails. Loaves are an add-on that can complete someone's תודה, but an animal is never brought just to complete someone's loaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? It makes sense that loaves come to complete a תודה. But does a תודה ever come to complete loaves?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the challenge and says the two cases are not alike.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves depend on the animal, so a person can sensibly vow loaves for someone else's תודה. The animal is the main offering and never serves the loaves. So the reverse reading from Step 8 makes no sense, and the answer of Step 7 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: 'How can you compare?' A phrase used to reject a comparison
Granted, it makes sense that...
To exempt or complete (Aramaic form of לפטור)

phrases.english: How can you compare?
Granted, loaves come to exempt a תודה,
but does a תודה come to exempt loaves?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי הַשְׁתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in Step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the רישא and the סיפא of the משנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The relationship only goes one way. Loaves depend on and complete a תודה, but a תודה never exists to complete loaves.
steps.whatToRemember: Loaves serve the תודה, never the other way around. That is why a vow for loaves can be read as 'for someone else's תודה', but a vow for the animal cannot be read as 'for someone else's loaves'.

steps.title: A ברייתא: one who vows a תודה without loaves is forced to bring both
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. Someone who vows a תודה without loaves, or an offering without libations, is forced to bring the full offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: someone who says 'It is upon me to bring a תודה without loaves,' or 'an offering without libations,' is forced to bring a תודה with its loaves, and an offering with its libations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to רב הונא (Step 4) and quotes a ברייתא. This sets up a challenge against him in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא teaches that a person cannot vow half of an offering. If he names the main offering, he must bring all of its required parts. The next step will draw an inference from the exact wording of this case.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal offering
Libations, the wine and flour offerings brought with an animal
We force him (the court compels him)

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who says "It is upon me to bring a תודה without loaves"
or "an offering without libations"
we force him,
and he brings a תודה and its loaves,
an offering and libations.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי תּוֹדָה בְּלֹא לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the discussion of the משנה's cases and returns to רב הונא's ruling, bringing a new source
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who vows a תודה without loaves, or an offering without libations, is forced to bring the complete offering.

steps.title: Inference: only saying 'תודה' forces him, which challenges רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא forces him only because he said 'תודה'. That implies a vow of just 'loaves' would not force him to bring the animal, against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason he is forced is that he said 'תודה.' But if he did not say 'תודה', he would not be forced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely and finds a hint that seems to disagree with רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's case works because the person named the main offering, the תודה. So if someone named only the loaves, he would not be forced to bring the animal. רב הונא said that a vow for 'loaves of a תודה' requires the animal too, so this inference seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The reason is because...' A phrase that sets up an inference from what the source left out

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא never says anything directly about vowing loaves. The challenge to רב הונא comes only from an inference: 'it worked because he said תודה', so it would not work without that word.

phrases.english: The reason is that he said [תודה],
phrases.notes: The word תודה isn't actually in the Aramaic here; it's filled in from the end of the line.

phrases.english: but if he did not say תודה, no.
phrases.notes: He means: if he vowed only the loaves, we would not force him to bring the animal.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּאָמַר, אֲבָל לָא אָמַר תּוֹדָה – לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the inference from the ברייתא quoted in Step 10 and aims it at רב הונא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling (Step 4) that a vow for 'loaves of a תודה' requires bringing the animal as well
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forces the full offering only because the person said 'תודה'. That implies a vow naming only the loaves would not require the animal, which contradicts רב הונא.

steps.title: The ברייתא said 'תודה' only to match its parallel case
steps.stepSummary: Even a vow of just 'loaves' would force him to bring the animal. The ברייתא said 'תודה' only because its parallel case about libations could not be phrased the other way around.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the same rule applies even if he never said 'a תודה.' But since the ברייתא wanted to teach 'an offering without libations,' and could not teach that case as 'libations without an offering,' it also phrased the first case as 'a תודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the inference from step 11. The word 'תודה' in the ברייתא is not there to exclude a vow of just loaves; it is there for parallel style.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 11 read meaning into the word 'תודה.' Here the גמרא explains that the ברייתא needed to phrase the libations case as 'offering without libations,' because libations can be vowed on their own. To keep both cases parallel, it phrased the first case as 'תודה without loaves' too. So nothing can be inferred against רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: The same rule applies
Since / because (it was teaching one case, it phrased the other the same way)
An animal offering
Libations (wine, flour and oil brought with an offering)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think libations are like loaves here. Loaves of a תודה cannot be vowed on their own, but libations can. That is exactly why the ברייתא could not say 'libations without an offering.'

phrases.english: The same is true
even though he did not say "a thanks offering"
and since the tanna wants to teach
"an offering without libations"
which he cannot teach as "libations without an offering"
phrases.notes: Libations can be brought by themselves, so vowing 'libations' alone is a normal, valid vow. That's why it couldn't be phrased this way.

phrases.english: he also taught "a thanks offering"

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא הַדִּין אַף עַל גַּב דְּלָא אָמַר תּוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inference of step 11 and defends רב הונא
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The inference drawn from the word 'תודה' in the ברייתא
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word 'תודה' is there for parallel phrasing with the libations case, not to exclude a vow of loaves alone

steps.title: Why force him if his vow carries its own reason to be cancelled
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא itself: why force the vower, when his mistaken vow seems to contain a built-in reason for cancellation?
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is he forced? This is a vow that comes with its own opening for release!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now attacks the ruling of the ברייתא from step 10. It asks why the vower should be forced to bring the full offering at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man vowed a תודה without loaves, thinking that was possible. Once he learns it is not, he can say 'I never would have vowed this.' That built-in regret should cancel the vow entirely, not force him into a bigger obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Why?
A vow that carries its own 'opening,' a built-in reason for cancellation
An 'opening': a reason to release a vow

phrases.english: Why?
It is a vow with its opening along with it!
phrases.notes: 'Opening' means a ready way out of the vow. He can say, 'Had I known you can't bring a תודה without loaves, I'd never have vowed.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמַּאי? נֶדֶר וּפִתְחוֹ עִמּוֹ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the ברייתא of step 10 and challenges its ruling directly
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that the vower is forced to bring the full offering
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A vow based on a mistaken idea carries its own reason for cancellation, so it should be void, not enforced

steps.title: חזקיה: the ברייתא follows בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה says the ברייתא follows בית שמאי, who hold that we go by a person's first words and ignore the contradicting words that follow.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: Whose view is this? It is בית שמאי, who say: hold on to the first words. As the משנה teaches: 'I am a נזיר from dried figs and pressed figs.' בית שמאי say he is a נזיר, and בית הלל say he is not a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: חזקיה answers the question by saying the ברייתא follows only בית שמאי. He proves their view from a משנה about נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בית שמאי, the first words 'a תודה' are binding, and the added 'without loaves' is ignored. So the vow is not cancelled. The same thing happens in the case of 'a נזיר from figs': the first words 'I am a נזיר' count. בית הלל disagree, so by this answer the ברייתא does not follow the accepted view.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose opinion is this?
Hold on to the first words; the later contradicting words are ignored
One who vows to abstain from wine and grape products
Dried figs
Pressed figs (a fig cake)

steps.whyThisMatters: Since the הלכה usually follows בית הלל, this answer leaves the ברייתא as a minority view. The next step brings רבי יוחנן's answer, which fits it with בית הלל.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:
Whose opinion is this?
It is Beit Shammai,
who say: Hold on to the first statement.
As we learned: "I am hereby a nazirite
from dried figs and from pressed figs"
phrases.notes: Figs aren't forbidden to a נזיר at all, so the second half of his words contradicts the first half.

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: He is a nazirite,
and Beit Hillel say: He is not a nazirite.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: הָא מַנִּי? בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13 by assigning the ברייתא to בית שמאי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the source to a specific opinion
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vow should be cancelled because it was made under a mistake
steps.terutzMaskana: According to בית שמאי the first words bind and the contradicting addition is ignored, so the vow stands

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: even בית הלל agree when he says he would have vowed properly
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the ברייתא can follow בית הלל too. The case is one where the vower says he would have made the proper vow had he known. He is forced only because he now wants to back out entirely.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say it follows בית הלל. The case is where he says: 'Had I known that one does not vow this way, I would not have vowed this way, but that way.' And what does 'we force him' mean? It is where he wants to back out.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a second answer that fits the ruling with בית הלל. He also explains why the ברייתא still uses the word 'forced.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no 'opening' to cancel the vow if the man himself admits he would have vowed a proper תודה with loaves. So even בית הלל agree the vow stands. Then the גמרא asks why force is needed, and answers that he now wants to retract completely, and the court does not let him.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (it fits this other view too)
We force him (the court compels him)
Backs out / retracts

steps.whatToRemember: A vow of 'a תודה without loaves' is enforced as a full offering. חזקיה says this follows בית שמאי ('go by the first words'). רבי יוחנן says even בית הלל agree, because the vower admits he would have vowed properly, and he is forced only because he now wants to back out.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says:
You may even say it is Beit Hillel,
where he says: Had I known
that one does not vow this way,
phrases.notes: 'This way' means vowing a תודה without loaves, or an offering without libations.

phrases.aramaic: לֹא הָיִיתִי נוֹדֵר כָּךְ, אֶלָּא כָּךְ.
phrases.english: I would not have vowed this way, but that way.
phrases.notes: 'That way' means the proper vow: a תודה together with its loaves.

phrases.english: And what is meant by "we coerce"?
Where he wants to retract.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא בֵּית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 13's question, avoiding חזקיה's need to attribute the ברייתא to בית שמאי
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only בית שמאי could enforce such a contradictory vow
steps.terutzMaskana: Even בית הלל enforce it when the vower admits he would have vowed properly. 'Forcing' applies only when he now tries to back out completely

steps.title: A second ברייתא: he says he never would have vowed, yet we force him
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that one who vowed a תודה without bread, or a זבח without נסכים, is forced to bring the full offering. This holds even though he says he would not have vowed at all had he known.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Someone says, 'I take upon myself a תודה without bread,' or 'a זבח without נסכים.' They tell him, 'Bring a תודה with its bread,' or 'a זבח with its נסכים.' He answers, 'Had I known that, I would not have vowed.' We force him, and say to him: 'שמור ושמעת.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about the same mistaken vow. This sets up a test for the two answers we just saw from חזקיה and רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the vower does not say he would have made the proper vow. He says he would not have vowed at all. Even so, the ברייתא says we force him, which sounds like going only by his first words, as בית שמאי hold.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal offering without the wine and flour offerings that normally go with it
Had I known: the vower's claim that he vowed by mistake
We force him (the court makes him keep his vow)
Observe and hear (דברים 12:28), said to the vower

phrases.english: Come and hear:
One who says: "It is upon me to bring a thanks offering without bread,"
or "an animal offering without libations,"
and they said to him: "Bring a thanks offering with its bread,"
or "an animal offering with libations,"
and he says: "Had I known that it is so,
I would not have vowed at all":
we force him,
and one says to him: "Observe and hear."

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: הָאוֹמֵר הֲרֵי עָלַי תּוֹדָה בְּלֹא לֶחֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new source to test the answers of חזקיה (step 14) and רבי יוחנן (step 15).
steps.raayaObject: חזקיה's view that the ruling to force the vower follows בית שמאי
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where the vower says he would not have vowed at all, and he is still forced

steps.title: This ברייתא fits חזקיה but seems to contradict רבי יוחנן
steps.stepSummary: The new ברייתא works well for חזקיה, who says the ruling follows בית שמאי. It is hard for רבי יוחנן, who limited forcing to a vower who would have made the proper vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to חזקיה it works out. But according to רבי יוחנן, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the new ברייתא matches חזקיה's answer but clashes with רבי יוחנן's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said that בית הלל would force the vower only when he says he would have made the proper vow. Here the vower says he would not have vowed at all, and we still force him. So רבי יוחנן's way of reading the case does not seem to work.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted: this works well for one view
It works out fine for him
It is a difficulty

phrases.english: Granted, according to Ḥizkiyya,
it works out well for him,
but according to Rabbi Yoḥanan it is difficult!

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְחִזְקִיָּה נִיחָא לֵיהּ אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא of step 16 to challenge רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that forcing the vower can fit בית הלל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forces a vower who says he would not have vowed at all. That fits only the בית שמאי approach of going by first words, not רבי יוחנן's case.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: this ברייתא really does follow בית שמאי
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן agrees that this second ברייתא follows בית שמאי. He still holds that the first ברייתא can fit בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן can tell you: This one certainly follows בית שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers by agreeing that this particular ברייתא follows בית שמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן does not change his reading of the first ברייתא. He simply says the two ברייתות are different. This one, where the vower would not have vowed at all, is בית שמאי. The first one can still follow בית הלל.

keyTerms.meaning: Certainly

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יוחנן is not taking back his answer from step 15. He admits only that this second ברייתא is בית שמאי. The first ברייתא can still follow בית הלל.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you:
This one certainly follows Beit Shammai.
phrases.notes: "This one" means the new ברייתא, where he says he would not have vowed at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָא וַדַּאי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the sources: each ברייתא follows a different view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both ברייתות must follow the same view, so רבי יוחנן's בית הלל reading falls
steps.terutzMaskana: The second ברייתא is בית שמאי. The first can still be בית הלל, in the case where he would have made the proper vow.
steps.whyThisMatters: This closes the discussion of how the ברייתא about vowing a תודה without loaves fits בית הלל and בית שמאי. רבי יוחנן's reading of the first ברייתא stands.

steps.title: What does 'שמור ושמעת' mean here?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the פסוק 'שמור ושמעת' fits the case of the forced vower.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is meant by 'שמור ושמעת'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the words of the ברייתא itself and asks what the פסוק the court quotes means here. This sets up the answers of אביי and רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the court tells the vower 'שמור ושמעת'. The גמרא wants to know what each of the two words is telling him to do.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it? (a request for explanation)

phrases.english: What is meant by "Observe and hear"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁמֹר וְשָׁמַעְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the בית שמאי/בית הלל question and explains a phrase in the ברייתא of step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How each word of 'שמור ושמעת' applies to the vower

steps.title: אביי: one word for the animal, one for the bread
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'שמור' tells him to bring the תודה, and 'ושמעת' tells him to bring its bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: 'שמור': bring the תודה. 'ושמעת': bring its bread.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers by splitting the פסוק into two commands: one for the animal and one for the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, each word is a separate instruction. 'שמור' covers what he actually vowed, the animal. 'ושמעת' adds the part he tried to leave out, the bread.

keyTerms.meaning: Bring its bread (the loaves that go with a תודה)

phrases.english: Abaye said:
"Observe": bring the thanks offering;
"and hear": bring its bread.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי שְׁמֹר הָבֵא תּוֹדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שמור' means bring the תודה; 'ושמעת' means bring the bread.

steps.title: רבא: bring everything, and don't make a habit of such vows
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that 'שמור' means bring the תודה with its bread. 'ושמעת' is a warning not to make vows like this regularly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: 'שמור': bring the תודה and its bread. 'ושמעת': you should not be used to doing this.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different explanation. The first word covers the whole offering, and the second word is a warning for the future.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבא, 'שמור' already requires both the animal and the bread together. 'ושמעת' is then free to teach a lesson: don't get used to making such careless vows.

keyTerms.meaning: Used to, in the habit of
To do so (to make vows this way)

steps.whatToRemember: The court forces the vower and tells him 'שמור ושמעת'. אביי reads it as two commands: animal and bread. רבא reads it as one command for the whole offering, plus a warning not to vow like this again.

phrases.english: Rava said:
"Observe": bring the thanks offering and its bread;
"and hear": that you should not be accustomed
to act this way.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר שְׁמֹר הָבֵא תּוֹדָה וְלַחְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to step 19, disagreeing with אביי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שמור' means bring the תודה and bread together; 'ושמעת' warns him not to make a habit of such vows.

steps.title: Must a תודה vowed from מעשר money really come from מעשר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: one who vows a תודה and its bread from מעשר money 'shall bring' it that way. It asks whether he truly has no choice but to bring it from מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'A תודה and its bread from מעשר': he shall bring it. 'He shall bring'? Must he really bring it that way?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It questions the word 'יביא', which sounds like a requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's wording sounds as if he is required to use מעשר money because he said so. The גמרא asks whether that can be right: shouldn't he also be able to pay with regular money?

keyTerms.meaning: Here, מעשר שני money, which must be spent in ירושלים
He shall bring
Is it not enough unless...? (is there no other way?)

phrases.english: "A thanks offering, it and its loaves from tithe money":
he shall bring it.
phrases.notes: This is a line from our משנה.

phrases.english: "He shall bring"?
Is there no way but that he brings it so?
phrases.notes: He means: must he really use מעשר money? Surely regular money would be fine too.

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹדָה הִיא וְלַחְמָהּ מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר יָבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'יביא' sounds like a requirement to use מעשר money, but there seems to be no reason to force that. Regular money should work too.

steps.title: רב נחמן and רב חסדא: using מעשר money is his choice
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב חסדא explain that 'יביא' means he may bring it from מעשר if he wishes. He is not required to.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן and רב חסדא say: If he wants, he brings it from מעשר. If he does not want, he does not bring it from there.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים answer that the משנה gives permission, not a requirement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'יביא' is read as 'he may bring'. Using מעשר money is allowed, but he can also pay with regular money.

keyTerms.meaning: If he wants, he brings
If he does not want, he need not bring it that way

steps.whatToRemember: In the משנה, 'יביא' about a תודה from מעשר money means he is allowed to use מעשר, not required to.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman and Rav Ḥisda say:
if he wants, he brings it from tithe money;
if he does not want, he does not bring it from there.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב נַחְמָן וְרַב חִסְדָּא אָמְרִי רָצָה מֵבִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה's wording: permission, not obligation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'יביא' means he must use מעשר money
steps.terutzMaskana: 'יביא' means he may use מעשר money if he wants

steps.title: The next line of the משנה about the bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: the bread may not come from מעשר שני wheat, only from מעשר שני money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The person may not bring the bread from wheat that is מעשר שני. He must bring it from מעשר שני money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up the discussion that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה separates two things: the actual מעשר שני wheat, and money that has the status of מעשר שני. The bread may not come from the wheat itself, but may be bought with the money. The next steps will ask exactly how far this rule goes.

keyTerms.meaning: The second tithe, food that must be eaten in ירושלים
Wheat of
Money (coins) of

phrases.english: And he may not bring it from second-tithe wheat,
phrases.notes: "It" means the bread that goes with the תודה.

phrases.english: rather, from second-tithe money.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא יָבִיא מֵחִיטֵּי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same משנה quoted in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The bread of the תודה is not brought from מעשר שני wheat, only from מעשר שני money.

steps.title: Only the actual tithe wheat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן and רב חסדא limit the משנה: only actual מעשר שני wheat is forbidden, but wheat bought with מעשר שני money may be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן and רב חסדא both say: The משנה only forbids wheat that is itself מעשר שני. But wheat that was bought with מעשר שני money may be used for the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: Two אמוראים explain how narrow the משנה's rule is. The ban covers only the wheat that was the tithe itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasted "מעשר שני wheat" with "מעשר שני money." Wheat bought with that money falls in between, and רב נחמן and רב חסדא put it on the allowed side, together with the money.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about... (a phrase that limits a rule)
That were bought
Both of them

phrases.aramaic: רַב נַחְמָן וְרַב חִסְדָּא דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ:
phrases.english: Rav Naḥman and Rav Ḥisda both say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מֵחִיטֵּי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: They taught this only about second-tithe wheat itself,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מֵחִיטִּין הַלְּקוּחוֹת מִמְּעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי – יָבִיא.
phrases.english: but from wheat bought with second-tithe money, he may bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מֵחִיטֵּי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the scope of the משנה line quoted in step 24.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wheat bought with מעשר שני money may be used for the bread of the תודה.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה teaches the same rule before רבי זירא
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה, sitting before רבי זירא, says the same as רב נחמן and רב חסדא: bought wheat is allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה was sitting in front of רבי זירא and said: The משנה only forbids wheat that is itself מעשר שני. But wheat bought with מעשר שני money may be used.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story. רבי ירמיה repeats the same rule in front of רבי זירא, and this sets up רבי זירא's reaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the rule here; it is the same as step 25. The point of the story is to bring in רבי זירא, who is about to disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: Was sitting
Before him, in front of him
And was saying

phrases.aramaic: יָתֵיב רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya was sitting before Rabbi Zeira,
and he was sitting and saying:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מֵחִיטֵּי מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי,
phrases.english: They taught this only about second-tithe wheat itself,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל מֵחִיטִּין הַלְּקוּחוֹת בִּמְעוֹת מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי – יָבִיא.
phrases.english: but from wheat bought with second-tithe money, he may bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַבִּי יִרְמְיָה קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַבִּי זֵירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the ruling of step 25 in a story, setting up a disagreement.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ירמיה also allows wheat bought with מעשר שני money.

steps.title: רבי זירא disagrees: even bought wheat is not allowed
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא challenges רבי ירמיה and says even wheat bought with מעשר שני money may not be used.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said to him: רבי, you say that? I say that even wheat bought with מעשר שני money may not be used for the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא pushes back. He holds that the bread may not come from bought wheat either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי זירא, wheat bought with the tithe money is like the tithe wheat itself, so it is forbidden. Only the money may be used directly. This is a real argument against the view of steps 25-26.

keyTerms.meaning: You say so? (said in surprise)
Even
He may not bring

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the three cases: (1) the actual tithe wheat, which all agree is forbidden; (2) the tithe money, which all agree is allowed; (3) wheat bought with the money, which is what רבי ירמיה and רבי זירא argue about.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: רַבִּי, אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן?
phrases.english: He said to him: My teacher, do you say so?
phrases.notes: The one speaking here is רבי זירא, answering רבי ירמיה.

phrases.english: I say that even from wheat bought
with second-tithe money, he may not bring it.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי, אַתָּה אוֹמֵר כֵּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly disputes the ruling just said by רבי ירמיה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה's ruling that wheat bought with מעשר שני money may be used.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי זירא holds the opposite: bought wheat is forbidden just like the tithe wheat itself.

steps.title: רבי זירא begins with רבי ירמיה's reasoning: learned from שלמים
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא offers to explain both views, and starts with רבי ירמיה's: the תודה is learned from שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: I will say my reason, and I will say your reason. First your reason: Where do you learn the rules of the תודה from? From שלמים.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא sets up a full explanation of both sides. He starts with רבי ירמיה's side, saying the rules of the תודה come from the rules of שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי זירא is being fair: he will lay out his opponent's reasoning before his own. The source of רבי ירמיה's view is that a תודה is learned from שלמים. The explanation continues past this point.
